investigations.question: D5: Prove the strongest rigorous lower bound for N(H) = #{sorted solutions (a,b,c,d) of a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd with d <= H}. HARD CAP 500 words, symbol-dense lemma-proof style, no prose motivation, at most 2 one-line substitution checks. Take as proved (cite, do not reprove): the quotient mutation graph is a tree rooted at v0=(1,1,1,1); every non-root vertex's children are exactly the distinct sorted vertices obtained by mutating a, b, or c. SKELETON: (L-A, chain) v_j=(1,1,c_j,d_j), (c_1,d_1)=(1,3), c_{j+1}=d_j, d_{j+1}=4d_j-c_j. Prove by induction via the Vieta root-swap (state once: if (1,1,c,d) is a solution then (1,1,d,4d-c) is a solution) that all v_j are distinct solutions with d_j strictly increasing and d_{j+1}=4d_j-d_{j-1}, characteristic roots 2+-sqrt(3), so d_j = Theta((2+sqrt3)^j) and N(H) >= log_{2+sqrt3}(H) - O(1) with explicit constant. (L-B, branching lemma) Prove: every vertex at depth >= 2 has at least 2 DISTINCT children. Cases: if a<b<c, mutations at a,b,c give distinct new maxima since 4P/x - x is strictly decreasing in x; if exactly one tie among a,b,c, mutation at c versus at a differ since c>a (the unique vertex with a=b=c is v1=(1,1,1,3), which has exactly 1 child - verify). (L-C, counting) Full binary subtree below v2=(1,1,3,11): along any edge max' <= 4 max^3, so by induction log2(max) at depth t below v2 is <= 3^t (log2 11 + 1); the binary subtree contributes >= 2^t vertices whenever 3^t (log2 11 + 1) <= log2 H, i.e. t = floor(log3(log2 H/(log2 11 + 1))). Conclude N(H) >= c' (log H)^{log3 2}, log3 2 = 0.6309, with explicit c' and threshold H0. Final statement: N(H) >= max( log_{2+sqrt3} H - O(1), c' (log H)^0.6309 ), both constants explicit; note which dominates. If the branching lemma has a gap, isolate the exact failing case and prove the weaker bound it still yields. Anything stronger (e.g. (log H)^beta, beta > 0.631) must be labeled CONJECTURE with the precise obstruction.

investigations.question: Attack question:raised:07d805ce56d7:rq-sharp: is rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582 improvable toward the true growth rate of N(H)? HARD CAP 700 words, lemma-proof style. Take as proved (cite answer:work:003-struct-core-v2 and answer:work:004-upper-depth-v3, do not reprove): tree structure; children = mutations at a,b,c; child max >= (4ab-1)d; product ab nondecreasing along child edges; the a=b=1 locus is the single chain with ratio -> 2+sqrt3; N(H) <= C H^{ln3/ln11} + O(log H). ATTEMPT THIS ITERATED DICHOTOMY, proving each step that holds and labeling the rest CONJECTURE with the exact gap. (L1, level-p slow locus) For fixed a,b with p = ab, solutions (c,d), c<=d, of c^2+d^2 = 4p cd - (a^2+b^2) are generated by the Vieta involution (c,d) -> (d, 4p d - c) as one or more chains; each chain has consecutive ratio -> 2p + sqrt(4p^2-1) >= 4p-1, so contributes O(log H) vertices with d <= H. Prove the number of chains is finite by bounding each chain's minimal element (descend until d' >= d and bound that configuration explicitly); if finiteness resists, state it as the precise gap. (L2, product jump) At a vertex with ab = p: mutating c keeps product p (chain step, factor about 4p); mutating b gives new product a c >= c >= b >= sqrt(p) and in fact a c >= p c/b >= p when c >= b... establish the cleanest TRUE statement: any child strictly increasing the product has new product >= p^{3/2} (since the new product is ac or bc with c >= b >= sqrt(p)), hence per-edge factor >= 4 p^{3/2} - 1 below it. Verify the boundary cases a=b and b=c in one line each. (L3, iteration) Level 0: the ab=1 chain (O(log H) vertices); its product-raising children have p >= 3 (proved: u_j has ab = c_j >= 3). Level 1: vertices with ab=3, i.e. (a,b)=(1,3): equation c^2+d^2+10 = 12cd; find its minimal solution(s) and show the chains (u_2=(1,3,11,131) lies on one, ratio -> 6+sqrt35 = 11.92; substitution check 1+9+121+17161=17292=4*4323) contribute O(log H) vertices; their product-raising children have p >= min(1*c, 3*c) = c >= 11, so factor >= 43. Iterate: if level-k slow product p_k satisfies p_{k+1} >= p_k^{3/2}, then p_k >= 3^{(3/2)^{k-1}} (doubly exponential), each level contributes O(log H) chain vertices plus subtrees of size O(H^{ln3/ln(4p_k-1)}) whose exponents tend to 0. CONCLUDE the strongest statement actually proved: ideally N(H) = O_eps(H^eps) for every eps>0, stating exactly what the proof needs (finiteness of chain counts per level and uniformity of the level O(log H) counts); if full uniformity resists, prove the second iteration explicitly - N(H) = O(H^{ln3/ln43}) = O(H^0.2922), contingent on the ab=3 locus being a proved finite union of chains - and label the eps-statement CONJECTURE with the exact missing lemma. Phrase any lower-side bracket conditionally on the sibling lower-bound thread (N(H) >= c'(log H)^0.6309) since it is being proved in parallel. No tables; at most 2 one-line substitution checks.
